date.label: Undated Joshua allotment narrative
date.note: Biblical narrative chronology is not independently established as an absolute BCE date.

claims.claim: Seven tribes remain without territorial inheritance at Shiloh (Joshua 18:1–2)
Twenty-one men are appointed as three from each tribe to describe land (Joshua 18:4–9)
Simeon receives an inheritance within Judah’s region (Joshua 19:1–9)
Dan’s allotment tradition includes Leshem conquest and naming (Joshua 19:40–48)

connections.note: Judges 18 recounts a Danite migration and naming episode related to Joshua 19:47; event identity and sequence cannot be forced.
Pressure on Dan helps contextualize territorial difficulties.
Lot distribution principle precedes Joshua’s survey and allocation.
Earlier statement that Levites receive no territorial inheritance explains exclusion here.
The closing restatement that the LORD God of Israel is the Levites' inheritance (Joshua 13:33) confirms the same exclusion at the end of the allotment lists.
